key_insight: A mixed finite element discretization of the intrinsic Hodges beam formulation preserves structure while enabling natural boundary conditions and constraint-free multibody assembly.
engineering_relevance: This offers a numerically robust route for explicit multibody beam dynamics that avoids stiff algebraic constraints and can preserve energy in time integration.
method: Formulate beams in intrinsic variables using the Hodges description, which leads to linear differential operators.
Apply mixed finite elements so both kinematic and dynamic boundary conditions are imposed naturally.
Assemble multibody systems through port-Hamiltonian interconnections instead of algebraic kinematic constraints.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports demonstrations on multiple examples, including closed kinematic loops, and notes exact energy preservation with implicit midpoint integration plus fewer Newton iterations than prior energy-preserving schemes.
watch_item: The approach still depends on careful mixed-element formulation and time-integration choices, so implementation complexity and stability must be validated case by case.
paper_title: Mixed finite element discretization of intrinsic geometrically exact beams for explicit multibody dynamics
